source.title: A Training-Time Diagnostic for Generalization via the Log-Alignment Ratio

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small Transformers on algorithmic tasks and measures training and validation accuracy through memorization and grokking, directly testing the delayed-generalization behavior. It also adds a training-fraction sweep.
record.gate_note: The small-task accuracy and grokking outcomes are the direct results for V1. The paper also reports LAR trajectories and large-model overfitting diagnostics, but these do not test the other versions' specific claims about circuit formation, initialization or norm switches, delayed generalization in LLMs, efficiency thresholds, algorithm identity, or optimizer/numerical artifacts. Findings cited from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: It follows Power et al.'s setup: a 2-layer Transformer on 12 binary-operation tasks with AdamW and weight decay 1.0. It reports which tasks grok after memorizing, and runs a modular-addition training-fraction sweep. Those are direct results on V1. The LAR and 3B-pretraining results are diagnostics of a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that unembedding LAR tracks the memorization-to-generalization transition in grokking and predicts effective dimension via k≈n^{2(1−LAR)}. In 3B pretraining, its deviation from a non-overfitting baseline tracks the generalization gap, and its decline steepens before overfitting. They present it as a cheap, validation-free diagnostic and call the evidence correlational. They explicitly propose no new theory of grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Follows Power et al.'s small algorithmic-task grokking setup, with 12 tasks, a 50% split plus a modular-addition training-fraction sweep, and a primary focus on unembedding LAR. The paper does not state that it is an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking depends on task and training fraction: some tasks or fraction configurations do not grok. The reported training-fraction results do not identify the failing fractions or state exact grokking delays.

fits_no_version.finding: Unembedding LAR rises from ~0.5 and is lower at memorization than at grokking. Final LAR exceeds 0.65 for grokking runs and is ≤0.65 for non-grokking runs. kpred≈k95 at final checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weight–activation spectral concentration measure (LAR) separates memorizing from grokked states in algorithmic tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In 3B pretraining, 2/5 Adam and 3/5 Muon runs overfit. The LAR differential tracks the generalization gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unembedding LAR tracks overfitting in LLM pretraining without validation data.

record.problems: Small-task experiments use 5 seeds per configuration, and 4 of 12 tasks do not grok under the stated setup and budget. The text does not give exact grokking delays by training fraction or identify which two fractions fail to grok. The large-scale evidence is limited to 3B models, an internal corpus, and a 2B-token budget; the authors characterize the LAR evidence as correlational.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows were left out.

untested.parts: Whether test accuracy starts at chance is not separately reported. The criterion only requires validation accuracy below 50% at memorization.

missing.what: Per-configuration memorization and grokking epochs: e.g. addition 50% mem ep 40 / grok ep 200; 30% mem ep 40 / grok ep 520; modular division grok ep 180; x/y-or-x−y grok ep 2380; S5 xyx mem 320 / grok 760. Also the identity of the non-grokking fractions (5%, 10%).

record.verdict_notes: Grokking is used as a testbed, but the occurrence and timing results still bear on V1. Weight decay is fixed at 1.0 and never varied, so V5 is untested. The 3B runs show ordinary overfitting, not delayed generalization, so V4 is untested. LAR is not shown to anticipate the jump's timing, so it is not a V2 test.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not give exact grokking epochs for the training-fraction sweep or identify which two fractions do not grok, so the relationship between training-set size and optimization delay cannot be fully assessed.

The study tracks LAR and spectra, but does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit forming gradually, track removal of memorizing components, or test whether a progress measure predicts the timing of the accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic grokking experiment tests delayed generalization as a function of initialization scale or weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
The large-model experiments measure pretraining loss and overfitting, but do not test grokking-like delayed generalization on realistic data.
The study does not test whether low-norm bias selects an efficient circuit, or whether a critical dataset size or ungrokking follows.
The study does not compare the learned algorithms across runs or architectures.
The study does not test whether grokking is caused by adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax limitations, or whether controlling those choices removes it.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.size_stated: embedding dimension 128, feed-forward dimension 512, 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Train on the 12 binary operation tasks using a 50% train split; assess training and validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy through memorization and grokking
rows.baseline: At memorization: training accuracy >99%, validation accuracy <50%
rows.value: Tasks 1–5 and 10–12 grok reliably; grokking is defined as training accuracy >99% and validation accuracy >99%.
rows.note: The authors state that these eight tasks grok reliably. The figure reports mean accuracy across seeds, but exact grokking epochs are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Value is fine, but the delay can be read from the figures: memorization at ep 40–100 versus grokking at ep 180–2380 (Figs. 2, 21). The jump comes well after training accuracy saturates.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.size_stated: embedding dimension 128, feed-forward dimension 512, 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Train on the 12 binary operation tasks using a 50% train split, with a budget of up to 50,000 epochs.
rows.measure: Whether validation accuracy reaches the grokking criterion
rows.baseline: Grokking criterion: training accuracy >99%, validation accuracy >99%
rows.value: Tasks 6–9 do not grok with this setup and training budget.
rows.note: The text does not give individual task or seed outcomes.
rows.check: Correct as recorded. Tasks 6–9 (polynomial tasks) do not grok within 50,000 epochs at a 50% split.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.size_stated: embedding dimension 128, feed-forward dimension 512, 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Vary the modular-addition training fraction and measure validation accuracy during training.
rows.measure: Whether validation accuracy reaches the grokking criterion
rows.baseline: Grokking criterion: training accuracy >99%, validation accuracy >99%
rows.value: 2 out of 4 configurations do not grok; the text does not identify which fractions.
rows.note: This outcome shows that grokking is not obtained in every tested training-fraction setting. The text does not report the exact delay by fraction.
rows.check: The failing fractions can be identified. Fig. 2b labels 5% as non-grokking (final ep 50000), and Fig. 25b runs 5% and 10% to ~40000 epochs, so those two fail. 20% and 30% grok. Grok timing grows as the fraction shrinks: 50% at ep ~200 (Fig. 21a), 30% at ep 520 (Fig. 2a), 20% at roughly 2–3k (Fig. 1b axis clipped at 3× grok epoch). This matches V1, including no grokking within budget at very small fractions, so 'partial' understates it.

rows.subject: 2-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.size_stated: embedding dimension 128, feed-forward dimension 512, 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Measure unembedding LAR during training on the small algorithmic tasks.

conditions.value: 12 binary operation tasks at 50% train split and modular addition at 5%, 10%, 20%, and 30% train fractions

rows.value: Across the reported cases, LAR decreases briefly, then increases steadily and ends in the range 0.6–0.72; LAR at memorization is lower than at grokking, which is lower than at the final checkpoint.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 shows mean and ±1 standard deviation across 5 seeds.
rows.note: This is a reported training diagnostic, not a direct test of a circuit forming gradually or of the measure predicting the accuracy-jump timing.

rows.subject: 3B-parameter Gemma-2 models trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Measure training loss, validation loss, and unembedding LAR during pretraining.
rows.measure: Overfitting occurrence, assessed from training and validation loss
rows.baseline: 100B-token run is the non-overfitting baseline in the reported training budget
rows.note: The result concerns overfitting in pretraining, not a delayed generalization jump after training accuracy saturates; the count is reported in aggregate.

rows.subject: 3B-parameter Gemma-2 models trained with Muon
rows.operation_detail: Measure training loss, validation loss, and unembedding LAR during pretraining.
rows.measure: Overfitting occurrence, assessed from training and validation loss
rows.baseline: 100B-token run is the non-overfitting baseline in the reported training budget
rows.note: The result concerns overfitting in pretraining, not a delayed generalization jump after training accuracy saturates; the count is reported in aggregate.

rows.subject: 3B-parameter Gemma-2 models
rows.operation_detail: Compare unembedding LAR against the 100B-token non-overfitting baseline and compare the LAR difference with the generalization gap.
rows.measure: LAR differential and generalization gap over training
rows.baseline: 100B-token LAR; generalization gap defined as validation loss minus smoothed training loss
rows.value: The authors report that the LAR differential has a similar shape to the generalization gap; overfitting runs show steeper LAR declines as overfitting approaches.
rows.note: These are training-time overfitting diagnostics, not a test of delayed generalization in realistic LLM training.

relationships.condition: Tasks 1–5 and 10–12 at 50% split; modular addition at 20%/30% fractions
relationships.reason: Validation accuracy passes 99% well after the memorization epoch, and the grok epoch rises as the train fraction falls (~200 at 50%, 520 at 30%, ~2–3k at 20%); r1, r3. The epochs are read from figures.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy exceeded 99% well after memorization, with modular addition grokking around epoch 200 at 50% training data, 520 at 30%, and 2,000–3,000 at 20%.

relationships.condition: Polynomial tasks 6–9 at 50% split; modular addition at 5% and 10% fractions, 50,000-epoch budget
relationships.reason: These configurations memorize but never grok within budget, so grokking is task- and fraction-dependent; r2, r3.
relationships.display_finding: The polynomial tasks at a 50% split and modular addition at 5% and 10% training fractions memorized without grokking within 50,000 epochs.
